documents.title: General Obligations Law § 7-108 — Deposits made by tenants of non-rent stabilized dwelling units
documents.issuer: New York State Legislature (General Obligations Law, as amended by L.2019 ch.36 Part M, Housing Stability and Tenant Protection Act of 2019)
documents.notes: Prior to June 14, 2019, GOL § 7-108 contained only the applicability, successor-liability and anti-waiver provisions (now subdivisions 1-3) with no cap on the amount of a deposit and no deadline or itemization requirement for its return. The HSTPA (L.2019 ch.36 Part M, effective 2019-06-14) added subdivision 1-a: deposits capped at one month's rent, pre- and post-occupancy inspections, itemized statement and return within fourteen days, landlord burden of proof and punitive damages up to twice the deposit. Later amendments (L.2021, effective 2021-12-31; L.2022, revision 2022-03-04) added the seasonal-use and owner-occupied cooperative apartment exceptions (subdivisions 4-6); the text here is the current nysenate.gov revision dated 2022-03-04.

documents.title: Real Property Law § 238-a — Limitation on fees
documents.issuer: New York State Legislature (Real Property Law, added by L.2019 ch.36 Part M, Housing Stability and Tenant Protection Act of 2019)
documents.notes: Added by the HSTPA (L.2019 ch.36 Part M), effective 2019-06-14: application/processing fees prohibited except a background and credit check fee of the actual cost or $20, whichever is less; late fees only after five days and capped at $50 or five percent of monthly rent, whichever is less; waivers void. Subdivision 2-a (dishonored check fees) and the cooperative housing corporation carve-outs were added by later amendments (2021-2025); the text here is the current nysenate.gov revision dated 2025-10-17. Before 2019-06-14 there was no statutory cap on application or late fees.

documents.title: Real Property Law § 226-c — Notice of rent increase or non-renewal of residential tenancy
documents.issuer: New York State Legislature (Real Property Law, added by L.2019 ch.36 Part M, Housing Stability and Tenant Protection Act of 2019; amended by L.2024 ch.56 Part HH)
documents.notes: Added by the HSTPA (L.2019 ch.36 Part M § 3), effective 120 days after enactment, i.e. 2019-10-12: written notice of 30/60/90 days (based on occupancy or lease length) before a rent increase of five percent or more or non-renewal. Amended by the Good Cause Eviction legislation (L.2024 ch.56 Part HH) effective 2024-08-18 to require the notice to append the RPL § 231-c Good Cause disclosure; that version sunsets 2034-06-15, when the original paragraph (a) text revives. The text here is the current nysenate.gov revision (2025-08-22) and shows both versions of paragraph (a).

documents.title: Real Property Law § 227-e — Landlord duty to mitigate damages
documents.issuer: New York State Legislature (Real Property Law, added by L.2019 ch.36 Part M, Housing Stability and Tenant Protection Act of 2019)
documents.notes: Added by the HSTPA (L.2019 ch.36 Part M), effective 2019-06-14. Before that date New York common law (Holy Properties v. Kenneth Cole, 1995) imposed no duty on a residential landlord to mitigate damages after a tenant vacated early; § 227-e created that duty and voids lease clauses exempting it. No amendments since enactment (nysenate.gov revision 2019-06-28).

documents.title: Real Property Law Article 6-A — Good Cause Eviction Law (§§ 210-218)
documents.issuer: New York State Legislature (Real Property Law Article 6-A, added by L.2024 ch.56 Part HH; DHCR Required Notice as of February 19, 2025)
documents.notes: Article 6-A was added by L.2024 ch.56 Part HH, signed and effective 2024-04-20, applying immediately in New York City (§ 212) and to other municipalities only by local opt-in (§ 213); it is repealed effective 2034-06-15. The doc also embeds the DHCR Required Notice as of February 19, 2025 (https://hcr.ny.gov/good-cause-eviction-law-notice-february-2025) giving the FY2025 HUD fair market rents and the 245% thresholds for the five NYC counties (efficiency $5,471; 1BR $5,709; 2BR $6,321; 3BR $7,877; 4BR $8,499) and the 2023-to-2024 NYC-area CPI change of 3.79% (so the 2025 NYC inflation index is 8.79% and the local rent standard is 8.79%, below the 10% cap). DHCR republishes these figures each year on or before August 1; a newer notice dated May 4, 2026 exists and supersedes the 2025 figures for later leases.

documents.title: NYC Local Law 119 of 2024 — Fairness in Apartment Rental Expenses (FARE) Act (Admin. Code §§ 20-699.20 to 20-699.25)
documents.issuer: New York City Council (Int. No. 360-A, enacted as Local Law 2024/119 on December 13, 2024; adds Subchapter 15 to Chapter 4 of Title 20 of the Administrative Code)
documents.notes: Int. No. 360-A passed the Council 2024-11-13, was returned unsigned by the Mayor and became Local Law 2024/119 on 2024-12-13; by its § 2 it took effect 180 days later, on 2025-06-11. Before that date NYC tenants were routinely charged the landlord's broker fee; the law bars a landlord's agent (or any agent publishing a listing with the landlord's permission) from charging the tenant, requires fee disclosure in listings and a signed itemized disclosure before lease signing, and sets civil penalties and a private right of action. Text is the enacted Int. No. 360-A as published on Legistar.

documents.title: Real Property Law § 235-e — Duty to provide a written receipt
documents.issuer: New York State Legislature (Real Property Law; subdivision (d) added by L.2019 ch.36 Part M, Housing Stability and Tenant Protection Act of 2019)
documents.notes: Subdivisions (a)-(c) (written receipts for cash or non-personal-check rent, receipts on written request, three-year record retention, timing) predate 2019. The HSTPA (L.2019 ch.36 Part M), effective 2019-06-14, added subdivision (d): if rent is not received within five days of the due date the lessor must send written notice by certified mail, and failure to do so is an affirmative defense in a nonpayment eviction. A 2021 amendment (effective 2021-12-31) added the cooperative housing corporation mailing-method exception; text here is that current revision.

documents.issuer: New York State Homes and Community Renewal, Office of Rent Administration

Revision FS-16 (07/2025); effective_from is the revision month. effective_from set to 2019-06-14 (post-HSTPA content) so the sheet is retrievable for all post-HSTPA as_of dates; DHCR revision date was 2025-07-01.

documents.title: DHCR Fact Sheet #40: Preferential Rents
documents.issuer: New York State Homes and Community Renewal, Office of Rent Administration
documents.notes: Preferential rents after HSTPA: tenants paying a preferential rent on or after June 14, 2019 keep it for the tenancy, guideline increases apply to the preferential rent, and the legal rent may be charged only on vacancy. Revision FS-40 (05/2024); effective_from is the revision month. effective_from set to 2019-06-14 (post-HSTPA content) so the sheet is retrievable for all post-HSTPA as_of dates; DHCR revision date was 2024-05-01.
